financials.key_finding: onsemi's financial profile in fiscal year 2025 reflects the company navigating its deepest revenue trough since the El-Khoury transformation began, while simultaneously demonstrating that the restructured cost base and improved product mix sustain materially higher free cash flow margins than the pre-2020 commodity model would have allowed. Full-year 2025 revenue was $5,995.4 million, a 15.3% decline from $7,082.3 million in fiscal 2024, itself down from the $8,252.4 million peak in fiscal 2023. The compression was driven primarily by prolonged automotive semiconductor inventory digestion at tier-1 suppliers and a temporary moderation in SiC demand from EV OEMs recalibrating build plans. Despite the top-line pressure, onsemi delivered record free cash flow of $1,418.6 million — a 24.0% free cash flow margin — underscoring the capital efficiency of a business that had substantially completed its multi-year SiC fab investment cycle. The company returned 100% of that free cash flow to shareholders through share repurchases in 2025 and authorized an additional $6 billion buyback program in November 2025 to be executed over three years. On a full-year non-GAAP basis, gross margin was 38.4% and operating margin was 18.6%, reflecting the premium pricing of automotive-grade SiC and image sensor products relative to the legacy commodity mix. GAAP results were materially depressed by impairment charges and restructuring costs: GAAP gross margin was 33.1%, GAAP operating margin 1.4%, and GAAP diluted EPS $0.29 versus non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.35. The balance sheet as of December 31, 2025 showed $2,147.6 million in cash and equivalents plus $400.0 million in short-term investments, against $2,980.5 million in long-term debt — a net cash-adjacent position with conservative leverage given the free cash flow profile. The Q1 2026 trajectory represents a cyclical re-acceleration: revenue of $1,513 million beat the guidance midpoint, gross margin expanded for the third consecutive quarter to 38.5% (non-GAAP), and AI data-center revenue grew more than 30% sequentially. Management guided Q2 2026 revenue of $1,540–$1,640 million and full-year 2026 AI data-center revenue above $500 million.
structural_observations: Revenue base and cyclicality: FY2025 revenue of $5,995.4M represents a 27% decline from the FY2023 peak of $8,252M but remains approximately 60% above the pre-transformation FY2019 level of ~$5.5B, consistent with the thesis that El-Khoury's product mix shift raised the structural revenue floor. Q4 2025 revenue of $1,530.1M and Q1 2026 revenue of $1,513M establish a trough-to-recovery inflection; Q2 2026 guidance midpoint of $1,590M implies a return toward a $6.3–$6.5B annual run-rate, in line with sell-side consensus for FY2026.

Fiscal year cadence and segment seasonality: onsemi's fiscal year ends December 31 and the company reports four quarterly segments. Automotive end-market revenue (the dominant segment) typically shows seasonal strength in Q2 and Q3 aligned with North American and European automotive production schedules. The SiC and ADAS camera business lines exhibit a more linear demand profile given long-term supply agreements and model-year design-win cycles.

Margin progression and non-GAAP versus GAAP divergence: Non-GAAP gross margin has recovered from a 2025 trough near 37.6% (Q2 2025) to 38.5% in Q1 2026, with management targeting sequential expansion through 2026. The structural gap between GAAP (33.1% in FY2025) and non-GAAP (38.4%) gross margins is driven primarily by stock-based compensation, purchase accounting amortization on acquired intangibles (principally Fairchild Semiconductor, acquired 2016, and GTAT, acquired 2021), and restructuring charges. Investors and management focus predominantly on non-GAAP metrics for operating performance comparisons.

Capital structure and debt maturity profile: Long-term debt of $2,980.5M as of December 31, 2025 consists primarily of convertible notes at various maturities and drawn revolving credit. onsemi repaid $375M outstanding on its revolving credit facility at year-end 2025. The company retains approximately $1.5B of revolving credit availability. Net leverage (total debt minus cash) is approximately $433M, representing well below 1x trailing EBITDA — a conservative structure relative to semiconductor peers, providing financial flexibility to fund the buyback program and potential M&A.

Free cash flow as primary capital allocation metric: The company has consistently emphasized free cash flow over GAAP net income as its primary financial metric, consistent with the capital-intensive nature of its vertically integrated SiC manufacturing model. FCF of $1,418.6M in FY2025 on $5,995.4M in revenue (24% margin) compares favorably to the semiconductor industry median free cash flow margin. The $6B buyback authorization announced November 2025 — roughly 12% of the then-prevailing market capitalization — represents an aggressive capital return commitment.

Comparable peers and relative valuation context: Peer set includes STMicroelectronics (STM), Infineon Technologies (IFX), NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), Texas Instruments (TXN), and Wolfspeed (WOLF). Among power semiconductor peers, onsemi's FY2026 forward P/E of approximately 22–23x (based on non-GAAP consensus EPS near $2.60–$2.80) represents a moderate premium to NXP and STM but a significant discount to Texas Instruments and a large premium to loss-making Wolfspeed. EV/EBITDA of approximately 15–17x forward sits below the peer median for analog/power semiconductor companies, consistent with the market partially discounting automotive SiC demand recovery risk.

Market capitalization volatility and stock performance: ON shares traded at approximately $131–$135 per share as of late May 2026, implying a market capitalization of approximately $49–$51 billion. This compares to a 52-week range that reflected the stock's approximate 90% year-to-date rally from early 2026 lows as the AI data-center narrative gained traction and the automotive inventory correction showed signs of clearing. The stock's beta is elevated relative to the broader semiconductor sector, reflecting the EV-cycle sensitivity of its SiC revenue base.

leadership.key_finding: onsemi's leadership structure under CEO Hassane El-Khoury and CFO Thad Trent represents a tight-knit team with direct institutional memory of an analogous prior transformation — both executives served together at Cypress Semiconductor, where El-Khoury was President and CEO and Trent was CFO through the company's strategic pivot and ultimate $9.5 billion sale to Infineon Technologies in April 2020. This shared prior experience is a meaningful factor in the coherence and speed of onsemi's transformation: the duo arrived with a pre-existing operating playbook, interpersonal trust, and a network of relationships with automotive and industrial customer procurement teams. El-Khoury, 46, holds a BS in Electrical Engineering from Lawrence Technological University (2001) and an MS in Engineering Management from Oakland University (2006). He began his career as a senior design engineer at Continental Automotive Systems before joining Cypress in 2007. At Cypress he progressed through applications engineering, business development, and general management roles before being appointed CEO in 2016. His narrative at onsemi has consistently emphasized 'design wins, not design ins' — a phrase communicating a shift from transactional component sales toward multi-year platform commitments with strategic customers. Thad Trent joined onsemi as CFO in February 2021, one month after El-Khoury's December 2020 arrival. Trent first joined Cypress in 2005 and served as Cypress CFO from June 2014 through the Infineon close. At onsemi he has overseen the capital structure management — including the GTAT acquisition financing, the ongoing share repurchase programs, and the $6 billion buyback authorization of November 2025 — and is externally recognized as a credible long-term capital allocator, having been appointed to the board of directors of Lumentum Holdings in December 2025. The board of directors is led by an independent Chair, Alan Campbell, with the Chair and CEO roles separated — a governance structure onsemi adopted to provide independent oversight of the CEO and management team. The board includes directors with automotive industry operating experience, capital markets backgrounds, and semiconductor technology expertise. The DEF 14A proxy filed for the 2025 annual meeting (April 2025) provides detailed compensation disclosure: management compensation is heavily weighted toward long-term equity awards tied to relative total shareholder return (TSR) versus the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) and to non-GAAP EPS performance.
